newsitem.title: UK: United News & Media bids 372mln stg for HTV.
newsitem.headline: United News & Media bids 372mln stg for HTV.

text.p: British-based media group United News & Media Plc said on Friday it had agreed a 371.7 million pound ($618.1 million) bid for UK independent television operator HTV Group Plc.

United News, whose managing director Clive Hollick had been tipped to be eyeing HTV, ended weeks of speculation by announcing that it had agreed a 420p per share bid for the HTV shares it does not already own.
"...the directors of HTV unanimously intend to recommend HTV shareholders to accept the offer," the group said in a statement.
United News already owns around 29.8 percent of HTV and has received irrevocable undertakings to accept shares from HTV's directors representing around 0.7 percent of the company.

The acquisition of HTV will consolidate United News's position as a significant participant in ITV commercial television and the company said it expected "substantial synergies" through the combination of the two companies' television interests.
Roger Laughton, the chief executive of United Broadcasting & Entertainment, said United Media was keen to develop HTV's broadcasting and rights interests.
"There is a compelling strategic case for this acquisition which brings with it clear opportunities for cost savings and revenue growth," he said.
The deal will be broadly earnings neutral in its first financial year. The bid price represents a premium of around 27 percent to HTV's closing price on June 26.

News of the bid might disappoint rebel institutional shareholders in Yorkshire-Tyne Tees Television Holdings Plc, who are not supporting a recommended 711 million pound bid from media group Granada Group Plc in the hope of a counter bidder.
United News had been rumoured to be amongst possible bidders.
